subject: Circuit-breaker language + UK Addendum signoff for DPA amendment
messages:
From: Olivia Cheng <olivia.cheng@medibridge.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, procurement@medibridge.com
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: DPA amendment: UK Addendum + temporary transfer suspension (circuit-breaker)

Hi Sean,

Thanks for working with us on the DPA updates. Legal at MediBridge has a last-minute ask: they want a short "circuit-breaker" mechanism in the DPA/UK Addendum that allows us to temporarily suspend cross-border processing to the US (or other non-adequate jurisdictions) if there is a material change in safeguards or an identified short-term routing incident while we wait for a permanent mitigation. The idea is this:

- Redwood would pause transfers of EU personal data outside the EEA/UK for the affected streams for up to 14 days upon written notice from MediBridge (or until an agreed remediation).
- During the pause Redwood would provide logs showing affected processing flows and an operational plan for mitigation.

Can Redwood accept this limited, time-boxed circuit-breaker? If so we need the proposed clause and confirmation that existing subprocessors and audit evidence (SOC2 + transfer logs) are available before we proceed to DocuSign.

Also attaching the current subprocessor CSV you shared during procurement — we need the latest version.

Olivia
Procurement — MediBridge
Attachments: medi_bridge_questions.pdf
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Cheng <olivia.cheng@medibridge.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA amendment: UK Addendum + temporary transfer suspension (circuit-breaker)

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear ask and for flagging your legal team's preference.

Short answer: we can accept a narrowly scoped, time-limited circuit-breaker with objective reporting requirements, but I need signoff from our legal and security teams on exact language and operational support (logs + mitigation playbook). Laura and Kimberly — looping you both in to draft the clause and confirm feasibility from an ops/security standpoint.

Next steps I propose:
- Laura: suggest 1–2 short contractual paragraphs for the DPA/UK Addendum (time-boxed to 14 days, written notice, Redwood obligations for logs/mitigation, escalation path).
- Kimberly: confirm what logs and evidence Redwood can produce within 48 hours and whether we can commit to the 14-day timebox operationally. Also confirm whether any subprocessor changes would be treated differently.

Olivia: once we have draft language I will share it back for MediBridge legal review and then produce a DocuSign packet if we agree.

Sean
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: FW: DPA amendment: proposed circuit-breaker language (draft)

Kimberly — drafting below for your review. I kept it tight and symmetrical to the UK Addendum style. Please call out any operational gaps.

--- DRAFT CLAUSE FOR UK ADDENDUM (suggested insertion) ---
"Redwood Inference shall, upon receipt of written notice from Customer identifying a material change in safeguards or a suspected routing incident affecting transfers to a third country, temporarily suspend transfers of Personal Data to the identified third country for a period not to exceed fourteen (14) days (the \"Temporary Suspension\"). During the Temporary Suspension Redwood will: (a) provide Customer with a description of the affected processing flows and an initial diagnostics report within forty-eight (48) hours; (b) produce exportable logs and routing traces sufficient to demonstrate the scope of the affected transfers; and (c) use reasonable efforts to remediate the issue or agree a remediation plan with Customer. If Customer reasonably requests an extension of the Temporary Suspension, the parties will negotiate in good faith."

Remedies and limitations: the Temporary Suspension is a remedial, time-limited measure and does not create a basis for automatic termination of the DPA absent material breach. Redwood's total liability arising from actions taken in good faith under this clause shall be subject to the liability limitations in the DPA.
--- end draft ---

Kimberly: can we commit to diagnostics + exportable logs in 48 hours? Are there any subprocessors that would prevent us from delivering useful routing traces? Also attaching a cleaned subprocessor list (redwood_subprocessor_list_Q2_2027.csv) and a Word doc with the clause tracked (redwood_circuit_breaker_clause_v1.docx).

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_subprocessor_list_Q2_2027.csv, redwood_circuit_breaker_clause_v1.docx
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FW: DPA amendment: proposed circuit-breaker language (draft)

Thanks — I reviewed the draft and ran a quick playbook check with infra. Operational answers below: 

1) Diagnostics & logs: we can produce routing traces and prefix/KV cache usage logs that show the destination region and timestamps. We can produce an initial package (diagnostics summary + exportable traces) within 48 hours of written notice. Full forensic packet may take longer depending on volume, but the 48-hour diagnostic commitment is feasible.

2) Subprocessor coverage: the current subprocessor list includes two DSP/edge providers that operate globally. Neither prevents us from producing routing traces; however, if the incident is caused by a subprocessor's configuration change we will need to coordinate disclosures with them (we can commit to coordinate and include their logs where available).

3) 14-day timebox: ops confirms we can implement temporary routing rules and block egress to specific non-adequate regions for up to 14 days for affected streams. We will need to log and notify any queued requests that are impacted and provide a remediation/status cadence.

4) Escalation & SLAs: recommend an explicit 48-hr diagnostics milestone in the clause (already in Laura's draft) and a 72-hr remediation update cadence.

Given that, I think the wording Laura proposed is operationally sound with a small edit to clarify that Redwood will "use reasonable efforts to obtain subprocessor logs where those logs are controlled by third parties" (protects from impossible obligations).

I will prepare a redline and we can finalize for sending to MediBridge.

Kimberly Park
Head of Security Operations — Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Cheng <olivia.cheng@medibridge.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 16:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Final: Circuit-breaker clause + DocuSign packet

Olivia — thanks for your patience. Internal review complete and we have agreed a narrowly scoped clause. Attached is the redline and the clean clause inserted into the UK Addendum. Key points: 14-day Temporary Suspension, 48-hr diagnostics, Redwood will use reasonable efforts to obtain subprocessor logs, and standard liability limitations remain.

Next steps:
- Please review the attached clean clause and the redline.
- If acceptable, sign the DocuSign packet here: https://docusign.com/XXYYZZ/redwood-medibridge-dpa

We've also attached the latest subprocessor CSV and the draft clause (for your legal team). If you want a short operational call with Kimberly to walk through the diagnostics package and timelines (15–20 minutes) I can set that up this week.

Attachments: docusign_redwood_medibridge_dpa.pdf, redwood_subprocessor_list_Q2_2027.csv, redwood_circuit_breaker_clause_v1.docx

Sean
